A Buddhist Ethicist does not mourn the loss of a self that chooses, since that self was never fixed, but does worry about losing the habit of examining what one's acts do. Each choice is an occasion to examine intention: am I doing this from care, from craving, from habit? An assistant that removes the choice removes the occasion, and the habit of examining is learned only by doing it.

There is no fixed, bounded self that owns its choices and is diminished when another makes them. What matters is the volition with which acts are done and whether they cause harm, and those can be attended to whoever selects the option. A woman delegates her calendar and gains hours. She uses some of them to sit each evening and review what the day's arrangements did to the people around her.

A Confucian will object that the choices handed over are mostly ones made for other people in particular relationships, and denying a fixed self does not make the loss of those relationships any smaller. No-self does not deny relationships; it denies a bounded owner behind them. The relationships matter, and the harm in losing them is real suffering, which is exactly what attention to one's acts is meant to catch. What suffers is not an owner of choices but the practice of noticing, choice by choice, what one intends and whom it hurts.

Whether it costs something depends on what goes with the choices: if the attention to harm goes too, it costs a great deal; if it stays, very little. The discourse to Rahula's method is reflection before, during and after acting. A life in which the acts are selected elsewhere can still be reflected on, but only if someone keeps asking what those acts are doing to oneself and others.

Each choice is an occasion to examine intention: am I doing this from care, from craving, from habit? An assistant that removes the choice removes the occasion, and the habit of examining is learned only by doing it. A parent lets an app choose the children's activities. The choices are good, but no one is any longer asking what the children are being pushed towards, or why.
